title: Prop Sheet flow - animals and props, two ratios and a placement axis
description:
A second sheet flow, SEPARATE from the Character Sheet (MPI-504) by Fabio's call 2026-08-20: "Either we have a separate flow for it, which is probably the best idea, or we include it into the character sheet. I think it's best to have a separate flow for it." Same family, same machinery, different subject and different controls.

WHAT IT MAKES. Reference sheets for ANIMALS and PROPS rather than people - the kind already in the 'The Failed Heist' project: a saddled horse in two views (side + front) on flat grey, a black hat from two angles, revolvers and lever-action rifles laid out, a wagon with its team. Fabio's screenshot of that project is the spec: several views of ONE object in one continuous frame, plain grey studio backdrop, flat even light, no grain and no lens character - the same 'keep the sheet boring' rule the Character Sheet inherits from the Higgsfield brief, and for the same reason (a look baked into the reference is carried into every shot the asset appears in).

THREE DIFFERENCES FROM MPI-504, and they are the whole card:

1. NO HEADLESS PASS. The front-body head removal exists because a video model sources a face from the smallest figure on the sheet. A horse or a hat has no such failure, so the whole SAM3 + Klein masking branch drops out. That also means the flow needs only krea2 - no klein-4b, no face-yolov8n, no Impact/SAM3 chain - which makes it cheaper to install and much simpler to wire.

2. TWO RATIOS, USER-CHOSEN: 8:5 AND 16:9. MPI-504 fixed 8:5 because three human panels need the height. A prop laid out along its length (a rifle, a wagon) wants 16:9. So this flow exposes a real ratio control - and it hits the SAME gap MPI-504 hit: one declared field emits ONE value, and the graph needs TWO nodes (Input_Width + Input_Height). Read MPI-504's plan.md `## Plan Drift` before designing it; the three options are recorded there and this card should reuse whichever MPI-504 settles on rather than inventing a second answer. NOTE the 8:5 values moved on 2026-08-20: FLUX_RATIOS 1k is now 1280x800 (was 1280x768, which was really 5:3), and krea2 2k is 1792x1120.

3. A PLACEMENT CONTROL, WITH GUIDANCE. Fabio: "it should also allow the user to select how the prop is placed, with some instructions on what works best." This is the flow's distinctive control and it does not exist anywhere yet. It is a prompt-recipe axis exactly like Input_Recipe - a bank of template strings behind an MpiAnySwitch on an int - naming how the object sits in frame: side profile + front, three-quarter turnaround, laid flat from above, standing/upright, held-or-worn. Each option needs an `info` saying what it suits, because the right placement is object-dependent and the user cannot be expected to guess: a rifle reads along its length, a hat needs a three-quarter to show the crown, a saddled horse wants side + front. Fabio's own generations are the evidence base for which placements actually work - harvest them before writing the bank.

WHAT IT INHERITS UNCHANGED. The Character Sheet's whole app half is reusable and should NOT be re-derived: the `promptEnhance` universal op (recipe injected by the caller, so this flow supplies its OWN prop-oriented recipe rather than registering a twin op), the prompt-pair UI (`docs/playbooks/add-flow/ui/prompt-enhance.md` - user prompt, Enhance button, editable enhanced phrase, the sidecar storing both), the `kind: 'fields'` refine step, and the style axis if a prop sheet wants one. The enhancer RECIPE is the part that must be rewritten: MPI-504's writes a person (age, wardrobe, hair, eyes) and would produce nonsense for a wagon.

BUILD ORDER. This card should NOT start before MPI-504's flow has had a live run - it inherits MPI-504's graph shape, its ratio answer and its prompt UI, and starting early means building on three unsettled things. Graph is authored at the bench by Fabio (comfy_workflows/raw/ is user-owned), then /mpi-add-flow for the app half.

UMBRELLA: MPI-560 - The Flow track. Sits beside MPI-504 in the same phase; the sheet family is the keystone the swap/asset work consumes.
